- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20d moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above 30d true mean, adjust down by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For horizon >15d, model tends to lag true price by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model overfits short-term sentiment; use 5-day sentiment average instead of raw history.
